chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Ibn Muskān, from Abū Baṣīr, from Abū al-Ḥasan (peace be upon him), who said:

When my father was near death, he said to me, 'O my son, he who轻视s prayer will not attain our intercession, and he who is addicted to these drinks will not drink from our basin (al-Ḥawḍ).' I said, 'O my father, and which drinks?' He said, 'Every intoxicant.'

key_terms.اَلْحَوْضَ: the basin (of the Prophet/Imams on Judgment Day)
key_terms.اُحْتُضِرَ: was near death / was in the throes of death

ai.seo_question: What are the two main sins that prevent one from attaining the intercession of the Imams according to this hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this deathbed narration from Imam al-Bāqir (peace be upon him) to his son Imam al-Ṣādiq (peace be upon him) establishes a direct causal link between the neglect of Ṣalāh and the addiction to intoxicants as primary barriers to receiving Ahl al-Bayt’s intercession (shafāʿah) and drinking from their basin (ḥawḍ). By defining 'these drinks' as 'every intoxicant' (kull muskiran), the Imam provides a comprehensive juristic criterion that extends beyond wine to include all substances causing intoxication, reinforcing the principle of *jamʿ al-ṣalāh wa al-khamr* (the combination of prayer and wine) as a disqualifier for spiritual proximity.
